blocks.content: ETHAN
She laughed with me instead of at me. There's a difference. The difference was dangerous.

blocks.speaker: Cassandra
blocks.content: Well, technically Ethan — I think it's good.
I looked at the canvas because looking at her directly felt like trying to sketch something that keeps moving.

blocks.speaker: Ethan
blocks.content: It's not finished.

blocks.speaker: Cassandra
blocks.content: Most good things aren't.
Easy sentence. She said it like she wasn't paying much attention to it. But it landed the way things land when they're actually true — not with a sound, just with weight.
I looked at her then. For a second she wasn't smiling — a very small gap, barely anything — and then it came back so fast I almost convinced myself I'd imagined the pause.
She held up the dinosaur.

blocks.speaker: Cassandra
blocks.content: This is Winston.

blocks.speaker: Ethan
blocks.content: Of course it is.

blocks.speaker: Cassandra
blocks.content: He's been through a lot.

blocks.speaker: Ethan
blocks.content: He looks like it.

blocks.speaker: Cassandra
blocks.content: Rude, but accurate.
A laugh came out of me before I could decide whether to let it. She looked like she'd won a small game I hadn't known we were playing.

blocks.speaker: Lena
blocks.content: Cass! We're going to be late.

blocks.speaker: Cassandra
blocks.content: Late for what?

blocks.speaker: Lena
blocks.content: You said you were starving.

blocks.speaker: Cassandra
blocks.content: I say a lot of things.

blocks.speaker: Lena
blocks.content: That's true and also a problem.
Cassandra looked back at me. I was doing something with my hands. I don't know what.

blocks.speaker: Cassandra
blocks.content: I have to go before my friend stages a formal intervention.

blocks.speaker: Ethan
blocks.content: That sounds serious.

blocks.speaker: Cassandra
blocks.content: She's very committed.
I nodded. I had nothing else.

blocks.speaker: Cassandra
blocks.content: You should finish it.

blocks.speaker: Ethan
blocks.content: I was planning to.

blocks.speaker: Cassandra
blocks.content: And make the fountain a little less sad.

blocks.speaker: Ethan
blocks.content: That might be dishonest.

blocks.speaker: Cassandra
blocks.content: Artists are allowed to be hopeful.
Then she turned and jogged toward Lena. I watched her go. Didn't pretend otherwise.
At the archway she looked back once. Not long — just enough that I knew it was on purpose.
Then she was gone.
I stood there with paint on my knuckle and the very specific feeling of a day that had tilted somewhere new without asking permission.
She talked to me. I know how that sounds. I know.
I went back to the canvas. Made the light warmer. Made the fountain a little less sad.
